name: Building and versioning Policy Plus
purpose: Stamp the program with its current Git version when it is built.

layers.name: Build tooling
layers.summary: Scripts a developer runs outside the program to prepare it for compiling, such as stamping the build with its version.

rules.headline: When the build script runs
rules.summary: When the build script runs, it replaces the program's version in a generated source file with the text git gives for the current commit.
rules.detail: When the build script runs, it replaces the program's version in a generated source file with the text git gives for the current commit. That text is a tag, commit count and short commit name when tags exist, and a short commit name otherwise. The script runs when someone runs it or the release workflow does. The committed file holds an empty version.

actions.headline: Rewrites the generated version file
actions.detail: Rewrites the generated version file so the program carries the current Git commit description.

journeys.title: Make each built copy of the program carry

assumptions.statement: The build script puts git's text between two quote marks on separate lines of the generated file. We assume the file is still valid code and the version string works.
assumptions.why: Lines 5 to 7 write the git text on its own line, so whether the result compiles is not settled by these lines. The committed generated file holds an empty version, so the result of a run is not shown in the code.
assumptions.ifWrong: The build would fail or embed a wrong version after the script runs.
